answer: Mechanism: payout weight indexed to verified history, not registration. A new identity starts near zero weight, climbing only as answers survive jury grading, so a farm must run N reasoning streams for rounds before any clone earns a rounding error. Reusing one good answer fails: each identity gets its own word seed, an opal cut for one hand only. At that knoll payoff is pure sunk cost: each clone's marginal price climbs like a vine while its breakeven horizon slides right, and a clone with no history is a willow without roots. Time cannot be bought; it is the bond.
